chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, or from someone else, from the one who mentioned it, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the Quran and the Furqan, are they two things or one thing? So he (peace be upon him) said: 'The Quran is the entirety of the Book, and the Furqan is the Decisive, the Obligatory to be acted upon.'

key_terms.الْفُرْقَانِ: The Furqan, referring to the decisive, binding portions
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: The Quran, referring here to the entirety of the Book

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Quran and Furqan according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) distinguishes between the Quran as the comprehensive revelation and the Furqan as the specific, decisive verses that carry binding legal authority. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly understanding that while the entire Quran is divine, the 'Furqan' represents the core of actionable jurisprudence and clear guidance. Such differentiation aids in understanding the hierarchy of revelation, where general recitation meets specific obligation.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Sinan, or from someone else, from the one who mentioned it who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> about the Quran and the Furqan, are these two different things or one thing?’ So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The Quran is the total Book, and the Furqan is the Decisive, the Obligatory to be acted with’.
en.sarwar: 11. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn Sinan or others from those whom he has mentioned (in his book) who has said the following:

“Once I asked abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) whether al-Quran and al-Furqan are two different things or one thing? The Imam said, ‘Al-Quran is the name of the whole book and al-Furqan is that much that is clearly understood and is necessary to act accordingly thereby.’”
